method: Sentence boundaries, patterns, bindings and context notes authored directly by the assistant after reading the corpus; no extraction script or NLP parser used for this file.

coverage.unit: One-based JSONL line number is one dialogue, not one sentence.
coverage.duplicates: Exact repeated dialogue train:33 points to train:20 inside this file. Repeated patterns in different contexts retain their observed bindings and notes; entries are not claimed to be globally unique templates.

runtime_registration: not_registered: these readable patterns are not CorpusTemplate runtime records

conventions.pattern: A whole sentence with explicitly named substitution slots. Substituting the supplied bindings reconstructs the reviewed sentence without opening a source file.
conventions.bindings: Observed fillers, not permission to substitute arbitrary words. Articles belong to the binding unless shown literally in the pattern.
conventions.repeated_slots: Repeated occurrences of one placeholder use the same binding. This represents an explicit lexical link inside the sentence, without consulting any source text.
conventions.grammar: Keep literal verbs, auxiliaries, particles, prepositions, negation and subject agreement. Replacement fillers must preserve the original syntactic category and number.
conventions.semantics: Surface patterns do not certify factual truth or completed actions. Desire, obligation, possibility, questions, reported content and conditional clauses retain their scope.
conventions.context: When present, describes unresolved references or omitted material. A source link cannot supply these at generation time; provide discourse context or explicit referents.
conventions.fragments: Retained as audit notes, not promoted to full-sentence templates.
conventions.source_text: Present only when the reviewed sentence differs from the input; the difference is explained in correction.
conventions.provenance: split, dialogue and turn are optional audit coordinates; numbering is one-based. They are not runtime dependencies.
